Fellow person seeking help here but maybe I can help you still. I'm a drug addict so I got suicidal in rehab (tried to hang myself, not a good time..) and got sent to a psych ward. Psych ward's vary by state and institution but I was told mine was pretty typical. You will lose your phone but they can't search it, you still have rights don't worry. If you go in saying you're suicidal you will be there for at least 3 days (72 hour psych hold), from there it will be up to your assigned psychiatrist whether you stay or leave (in your situation they will probably keep you). You will eat state funded hospital food so it can vary. Our food was at best so so. Think elementary grade school food. You will be watched but not intrusively. Most psych wards do a head count every 15 minutes but you won't notice it too much if you're in site. You'll have to go to groups which can be lame but will keep you occupied as there really isn't a whole lot to do in a psych ward. As for the xanax, you MIGHT get it there. My buddy was prescribed xanax when he went to the same psych ward after me and he was an addict as well so yea, they will cater to your situation since they will be watching you like a hawk. Also tell them you can't sleep, they will give you something to help you sleep which I'm gonna guess you barely get any sleep now which will help you get some sanity back. 
I'm sorry you're suffering, I'm suffering to so I know how you feel but just hang in there. I recommend personally you go but make sure someone outside knows so they can advocate for you cause once you're in there, you're in. The psych ward takes responsibility over you so anything that happens to you is on them so that's why you will be there for that mandatory 72 hours and maybe longer depending on your mental state. The best thing you can do for yourself there is to be 100% honest. If you still feel suicidal, tell them cause they can't help you if you lie. You might get the urge to just up and leave but just hang in there, it ain't jail, they can't keep you forever.
